Not on record: The welcome email has no record of a specific welcome offer or discount for new subscribers — owner should record: 'Welcome discount for new customers = [value or none]'.
Not on record: No record covers the scent profile or mood description of the lavender fragrance used — owner should record: 'Lavender candle fragrance note description = [e.g. fresh, floral, calming — as a product attribute, not a health claim]'.
Not on record: No record covers the candle's vessel or size (e.g. jar type, weight, or volume) — owner should record: 'Lavender candle container/size = [description]'.

Not on record: The Rose candle's catalogue description (f_57265414) lists only 'Soy wax' with no burn-hour figure. If the Rose candle also burns for 40 hours, the owner should record: 'product.rose_candle.burn_hours = 40 hours' so that claim can be made specifically about that product.
Not on record: No record explains WHY soy wax burns longer than paraffin in the owner's own words. If the owner wants to include that explanation, they should record a statement such as: 'Soy wax burns cooler and slower than paraffin, which is why our candles last longer.'
Removed "Khush Aamdeed — aap sahi jagah aaye!" — it names "aamdeed", which is nowhere in your records.

Left out: Walk the reader through what happens in the session — hair wash first, then treatment — so they feel prepared. — a process claim needs a record that can establish "process", and the one(s) cited cannot.
Not on record: What results or visible outcome does the keratin treatment deliver? (e.g. frizz reduction, smoothness, shine — record this against product.keratin_treatment so it can be stated in copy.)
Not on record: How long do the results last after one session? Record this as product.keratin_treatment.result_duration so it can be cited.
Not on record: Is there any aftercare the client should follow post-treatment? Record this as product.keratin_treatment.aftercare so it can be included in a welcome email.
Removed "The customer has a keratin appointment coming up." — it says something about the reader's own order or booking, and nothing here knows who is reading it.

Left out: Describes the treatment process — hair is washed first, then the treatment is applied — adds credibility and transparency. — a process claim needs a record that can establish "process", and the one(s) cited cannot.
Not on record: Which specific products or product brands are ammonia-free? The owner should record the product names or lines used so the email can name them specifically.
Not on record: Are there other services (beyond the keratin treatment) that also use ammonia-free products? The owner should record which services this policy applies to.
Not on record: Is there a booking link, phone number, or call-to-action URL the email should direct readers to? The owner should record the preferred contact or booking method.
Removed "There are no hidden charges" — No approved fact addresses hidden charges. The price fact states only the amount (₹3500), not whether charges are hidden or transparent..

Not on record: Whether the business automatically rebooks clients every month: the owner should record this as a confirmed policy, e.g. 'We automatically rebook every client on a monthly recurring schedule and notify them by email.'

Not on record: Does the 10% FIRST10 offer apply specifically to Desi Ghee 500ml, or to all products? Owner should record: 'offer.first10.applies_to = [product list or all]'.
Not on record: What is the origin or breed of cow whose milk is used? Owner should record: 'product.desi_ghee_500ml.milk_source = [e.g. Gir cow, A2 milk, etc.]'.
Not on record: Is the ghee made from cow milk, buffalo milk, or both? Owner should record: 'product.desi_ghee_500ml.milk_type = [cow / buffalo / mixed]'.
Not on record: Is there a shelf life or best-before period for the product? Owner should record: 'product.desi_ghee_500ml.shelf_life = [duration and unit]'.
Removed "Desi Ghee is made using the traditional hand-churned, slow-cook method called the Bilona process." — Approved facts state the Bilona method and hand-churned process separately, but neither fact describes the Bilona method as a 'slow-cook' method. The slow-cook element is not stated..
